newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest spot gasoline prices fall Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest spot gasoline prices fall Friday.

text.p: Prices for U.S. Northwest spot gasoline dropped Friday in reaction to eroding California values, while distillates eased on weaker regional demand.
"Demand for diesel is terrible up there," said a trader, referring to the Northwest market, which sees agricultural industry demand weaken in the autumn.

In California, bids for conventional-grade gasoline fell 0.50 cents a gallon to 58.50 cents a gallon, sparked by low regional retail prices, high stocks, and a fall in reserves compared to last year at this time.
Seattle conventional regular gasoline was talked between 1.50 and two cents lower at 57/58 cents a gallon.
Bids for Northwest low sulphur diesel fell 2.50 cents a gallon to 68.50 cents a gallon.
